name: Helix Biosystems Subdermal Whisper Node
description: The Subdermal Whisper Node is a surgically implanted near-field communication relay, roughly the dimensions of a large grain of rice, seated beneath the skin at the mastoid bone behind the ear. It transmits and receives audio communication via bone conduction directly to the inner ear, producing speech that the user perceives as clearly as their own internal monologue but which generates no external sound whatsoever. Transmission is handled through an induction coil that communicates with a paired external micro-relay unit — typically worn as a small adhesive patch on the jaw or collarbone — which handles actual RF transmission. The result is a communication system with no visible hardware, no audible output, and no behavioral tells beyond the operator's own discipline.

cultural_context: Helix Biosystems markets the Whisper Node with studied ambiguity — officially licensed for medical hearing augmentation and professional communications applications, with the licensing requirement theoretically ensuring accountability. In practice, the license is obtainable through several well-known back channels, and the device is standard equipment for anyone operating at the intersection of corporate intelligence and social infiltration. There is a sub-cultural cachet to the Whisper Node among high-end operatives: it represents a commitment to the craft, a willingness to undergo a surgical procedure for operational security. Those who use it are, by definition, people for whom invisible communication is a professional necessity rather than an occasional convenience.
known_users: Select law enforcement units authorized for covert surveillance operations
story_hooks: A player's Whisper Node begins receiving transmissions they never initiated — fragments of conversation in an unfamiliar voice, at irregular hours. The signal is coming from inside the pairing range.

Helix Biosystems quietly issues a recall notice for a specific manufacturing batch of Whisper Nodes, citing 'biocompatibility concerns.' Operators who have the affected batch implanted start comparing notes and realize the recall notice went only to them — not to their licensed installers.

An operative is found dead with her Whisper Node surgically removed post-mortem. Whoever took it wanted the implant, not what was on it — which suggests they know something about the hardware that isn't in any public specification.

A contact offers the players access to a Whisper Node that has been modified to record and store all received audio — a surveillance device disguised as a communication implant, already installed in someone who doesn't know it's been modified.
